channel.title: The Latin Wire
channel.description: Politics, business, entertainment, sports and culture for Hispanics

item.title: Kany García brings Puerta Abierta tour to the US
item.description: The Puerto Rican singer-songwriter brings her biggest tour yet stateside, opening September 7 in California and hitting 16 US cities through October.

item.title: Mourinho says he'll watch MLS after Messi's Argentina retirement
item.description: José Mourinho says fans must tune into MLS to catch Messi's final years after the Argentine great retired from international football.

item.title: Organizations across the US launch Hispanic Heritage Month 2026 programs
item.description: From Florida classrooms to Colorado fiestas, communities nationwide are marking Hispanic Heritage Month 2026 with scholarships, exhibitions, and cultural celebrations.

item.title: House passes bill to cut funds to colleges that boycott Israel
item.description: A bipartisan House vote to defund college boycotts of Israel raises durable questions about where campus autonomy, federal money, and free expression intersect.

item.title: AFA orders 10th-minute applause tribute to Messi at all matches
item.description: The AFA mandates a 10th-minute pause across all divisions to honor Lionel Messi, 39, after his retirement from international football.

item.title: Brazil and ECB study linking Pix to European payments platform
item.description: The ECB confirmed a preliminary study into linking its TIPS platform with Brazil's Pix, with a pilot possible by 2028.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump's August birthright citizenship executive order
item.description: A federal judge in Maryland on September 2 blocked President Trump's August executive order restricting birthright citizenship, calling it almost certainly unconstitutional.

item.title: Brazil and Paraguay to face Japan and Singapore in November tournament
item.description: A four-nation football tournament hits Singapore's National Stadium in November 2026, featuring Brazil, Japan, Paraguay, and the host nation.

item.title: Carney rejects Lutnick's account of collapsed trade talks
item.description: Carney says Canada will return to the table when Washington is ready, denying Lutnick's claim that Ottawa torpedoed talks for electoral gain.

item.title: Twin Minds Media adds five divisions to serve Hispanic market
item.description: The Miami agency splits into five named divisions covering PR, influencers, social, production, and events after a decade in the Hispanic market.

item.title: DOJ charges ICE officer Castro with false statements in Minnesota shooting
item.description: Federal prosecutors charged ICE officer Christian Castro with false statements over a January shooting in Minneapolis that occurred during the Trump administration's immigration enforcement surge.

item.title: Brazil's Senate approves critical minerals regulation bill
item.description: Brazil's Senate passed legislation Wednesday creating a legal framework for rare earths and other critical minerals, sending the bill to President Lula for his signature.

item.title: Judge hears arguments on extending USPS mail-ballot ban
item.description: A federal judge in Boston weighed whether to extend a block on a USPS rule implementing President Trump's mail-voting executive order.

item.title: Bipartisan House INSULIN Act introduced with two vulnerable Republicans
item.description: Five House lawmakers from both parties introduced legislation September 3 to cap out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 per month for privately insured patients.

item.title: Woodside and PEMEX sign MOU for deepwater Gulf of Mexico exploration
item.description: Woodside and PEMEX sign a non-binding MOU to explore deepwater Gulf of Mexico opportunities, building on their $7.2 billion Trion project.

item.title: The Warning to headline Mexico City's Estadio GNP Seguros in 2027
item.description: The Monterrey rock sisters are making history on multiple fronts, from Billboard charts to the biggest stadium stage in Mexico City.

item.title: Gloria Steinem, feminist activist and Ms. Magazine co-founder, dies at 92
item.description: Gloria Steinem's death at 92 closes a chapter in American civic life that reshaped how millions understood gender, power, and public voice.

item.title: Pemex launches international tender for high-spec jackup rig
item.description: Pemex wants a high-spec jackup capable of drilling to 30,000 ft, with bids opening in late September and a contract award set for October 7.

item.title: Musk's America PAC spends $800K on 2026 midterm races
item.description: Elon Musk's America PAC reported more than $800,000 in independent expenditures supporting Republican candidates across more than a dozen states.

item.title: Leon Black sues House Oversight, skips Epstein deposition
item.description: Leon Black filed suit to void two congressional subpoenas and skipped a scheduled deposition the same day.

item.title: Maduro and wife seek dismissal of US drug charges on immunity grounds
item.description: Lawyers for the former Venezuelan president and his wife argue a Manhattan federal court lacks jurisdiction to try them on drug-trafficking charges.

item.title: Ocasio-Cortez endorses Nixon in Florida Senate race
item.description: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez backed Florida Democratic nominee Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate on Wednesday, citing Nixon's grassroots funding record.

item.title: Wright signs Venezuela oil deals in Caracas, details emerge
item.description: Energy Secretary Chris Wright on September 2 oversaw corporate signings in Caracas as discrepancies emerged between U.S. and Venezuelan characterizations of the agreement.

item.title: Latino voters in Colorado and Pennsylvania shift on economy ahead of midterms
item.description: Poll shifts in Colorado and a competitive Pennsylvania valley raise old questions about Latino voting blocs, economic anxiety, and what actually moves elections.

item.title: Trump pledges 30-day campaign blitz for 35 Republican midterm races
item.description: President Trump announced plans to personally campaign in 35 competitive House and Senate races during the final 30 days before the November 3 midterms.

item.title: Minogue wins GOP primary, will face Healey in November
item.description: Minogue, a combat veteran and former medical device CEO, defeated Brian Shortsleeve Tuesday to claim the Republican nomination for governor.

item.title: US strikes Iran again as Trump rules out negotiations
item.description: U.S. Central Command completed a new wave of strikes against Iranian military targets on September 2 as President Trump ruled out negotiations.

item.title: Pentagon rules out troops at polls; DOJ orders states to report undocumented immigrants
item.description: The Joint Chiefs chairman tells a Democratic senator no troops will go to polls, while the DOJ expands immigration reporting requirements for states receiving federal welfare funds.

item.title: Appeals court reverses NLRB ruling on Starbucks NYC dress code
item.description: A three-judge panel directed the labor board to apply a more evenly measured balancing test when evaluating employer dress code policies.

item.title: WalletHub ranks Pembroke Pines top U.S. city for Hispanic entrepreneurs
item.description: WalletHub's 2026 report ranked Pembroke Pines first among more than 180 U.S. cities, citing the nation's highest Hispanic entrepreneurship rate.

item.title: AFA to pause all Argentina matches in Messi retirement tribute
item.description: The AFA will halt every domestic match at the 10th minute for a minute of applause after Messi, 39, announced his international retirement on Monday.

item.title: Smithsonian designates Arts and Industries Building for Latino museum
item.description: The Smithsonian Board of Regents has chosen a 145-year-old National Mall landmark as the permanent home for the long-awaited Latino museum.

item.title: DOJ opinion threatens welfare funding cuts over migrant reporting
item.description: A new DOJ legal opinion warns states they must report undocumented individuals to DHS or risk losing billions in TANF and SSI funding.

item.title: Brazil and Japan to meet again in Singapore tournament this November
item.description: Brazil and Japan renew their World Cup rivalry in Singapore this November as part of the four-team Mizuho Blue Challenge.

item.title: Paredes hints at Argentina retirement after FIFA ban and Messi exit
item.description: A 10-match ban, a $90,000 fine, and Messi's retirement have the 32-year-old Boca Juniors midfielder questioning his international future.

item.title: Supreme Court allows Trump White House ballroom construction to continue
item.description: The 5-4 ruling found the plaintiff likely lacks standing and did not rule on whether the $400 million project is lawful.

item.title: Ebrard meets Nvidia CEO and US commerce secretary at G20
item.description: Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard met Jensen Huang, Howard Lutnick, Sam Altman, and Tom Brown at the G20 Innovation ministerial in North Carolina.

item.title: Trump administration threatens to cut agency support for Smithsonian
item.description: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and White House Domestic Policy Council Director Vince Haley warned federal agencies may halt artifact loans, procurement support, and discretionary grants.

item.title: Paraguay midfielder Matías Galarza joins Inter Miami on loan from River Plate
item.description: The Paraguayan midfielder arrives on a one-year loan from River Plate, with a $3 million purchase clause tied to playing time.

item.title: Army Secretary Driscoll resigns after clashes with Hegseth
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll stepped down Wednesday after roughly 18 months, with sources citing blocked modernization efforts and friction with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
